title: Program 3: Nature-Graded
seed_question: Are the engine's odds on its own experiments still well calibrated when a quantum chip, not a language model, decides whether each bet passed?

qpu.cost_rule: 0.28 ms x shots + ~2 s/job; x1.5 for mid-circuit measurement

note: Converted from nature-graded map/program-3-map.md and .json (commit cb82b10, 2026-11-04 14:13 America/Denver). Engine odds stated before any data. No bets yet. The chip is the referee, never a computational resource.

directions.title: Does a correctly scheduled noise model close the Stage 1 gap?
directions.odds_event: The re-simulated Stage 1 circuit, scheduled ALAP with FakeFez durations and the job-time calibration, gives P(yes) ≥ 0.40. Control: the same model unscheduled must reproduce 0.25 ± 0.03, or the test is untestable.
directions.question: Once our simulator is set up correctly, does its prediction come close to what the chip actually did in program 1?
known: Program 1's circuit: the chip said yes 50% of the time, the simulator 25%, an ideal device 29%.
Our simulator let waiting qubits decay only if the circuit was timed step by step first; ours was not.
directions.cheapest_test: On a laptop, rebuild program 1's archived circuit, time every step as the chip would, load the chip's error rates from that day, and simulate it again; no chip time.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, P3-1

directions.title: Coherent or stochastic? Twirling and DD on the Stage 1 circuit
directions.odds_event: Arm (b), gate and measurement twirling, moves P(yes) toward the corrected-simulator prediction by ≥ 0.125 relative to arm (a), as run, at ≥ 3σ.
directions.question: If we randomly scramble the chip's errors, does program 1's result move clearly toward what the corrected simulator predicts?
known: Program 1 ran with no error scrambling and no idle-qubit protection: IBM's default turns both off.
IBM's published error rates are averages taken with scrambling on, which hides systematic error.
directions.cheapest_test: Re-run program 1's exact circuit on its original qubits in four interleaved versions (as run, random error scrambling, idle-qubit protection pulses, both), 2,000 shots each, plus readout checks.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, P3-2

directions.title: Is the gap nine particular qubits, or one afternoon?
directions.short: Bad qubits, or a bad afternoon?
directions.odds_event: On both pre-chosen alternative 9-qubit layouts, |hardware − sim| P(yes) is less than half the same-job original-layout gap.
directions.question: Run on two other sets of qubits on the same chip, does the gap between simulator and chip shrink to less than half?
known: One of program 1's nine qubits (no. 125) lost its quantum state much faster than the others that day.
Eight of the nine qubits read 1 less often than ideal, which argues against one bad qubit.
directions.cheapest_test: In one chip job, run program 1's circuit on two other sets of nine qubits picked by a rule fixed in advance, plus two repeats at least three hours apart.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, P3-3

directions.title: Does DD restore the missing entanglement?
directions.odds_event: Negativity with dynamical decoupling (XY4) on, minus negativity with it off, is ≥ 0.043 on item h088, with the bootstrap 95% interval of the difference above 0.
directions.question: Program 1's chip showed about half the entanglement the simulator expected; does protecting idle qubits bring a clear part of it back?
known: Program 1's measured entanglement was 0.147, 0.063 and 0.067, against 0.171, 0.149 and 0.118 simulated.
On this chip type, protection pulses cut how far noise models must be scaled up, from 3.6–4.0x to 2.3–2.5x.
directions.cheapest_test: Re-measure one entangled pair from program 1 (item h088) with and without idle-qubit protection pulses (dynamical decoupling), 1,000 shots per setting, interleaved in one job.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, P3-4

directions.title: Coherent or incoherent, from the archived tomography
directions.odds_event: Family (i), local unitaries plus a ZZ phase, beats family (ii), local Pauli channels plus global depolarising, by ΔlogL ≥ 10 on at least 2 of the 3 archived items.
directions.question: In program 1's saved chip data, are the errors clearly better explained as steady systematic twists than as random noise?
known: Program 1 measured three entangled pairs in detail (9 settings, 4,000 shots each); only one table was made.
IBM's reported error rates are averages that hide systematic error by design (McKay et al. 2023).
directions.cheapest_test: Fit program 1's saved measurements two ways, as steady systematic twists or as random noise, each with seven adjustable numbers, and see which fits clearly better; no chip time.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, P3-5

directions.title: Does ibm_fez leak settings between qubits?
directions.odds_event: Pass = clean: no pair has |δP| > 4.5σ after a Bonferroni correction over all pair-setting tests.
directions.question: Are this chip's qubits truly isolated, so that changing one qubit's setting never shifts what an unconnected neighbour reads?
known: Older IBM chips have shown such leaks (one pair shifted by about 5%), cause unknown.
A sister chip of the same type showed none; this chip, ibm_fez, has never been checked.
directions.cheapest_test: On about 40 pairs of neighbouring but unconnected qubits, change only one qubit's setting and check whether its neighbour's readout shifts: 4 circuits x 10,000 shots.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, P3-6

directions.title: Two-friend genuine local friendliness with external settings
directions.odds_event: S > 0 by ≥ 5σ at some n ≥ 1, on the single pre-registered facet (Bong facet 1) and labelling. In the same run, the decohered-friend control is consistent with S ≤ 0 and the no-signalling audit shows no deviation above 3σ.
directions.question: With a few qubits playing 'friends' who observe, does the chip break a limit that must hold if every observation is an absolute fact?
known: Only weaker versions, which reduce to ordinary Bell tests, have been run on quantum chips.
The strong version has been run only with photons, and it needs very clean states (purity at least 0.921).
directions.cheapest_test: Entangle two qubits, give each side a 'friend' of 0 to 4 qubits, fix settings from a public random beacon, and run 9 setting pairs, 2,500 shots each, plus controls.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, P3-7

directions.title: Is there a one-friend genuine LF inequality?
directions.odds_event: A non-Bell local-friendliness facet exists in the one-friend 3×2 or 3×3 scenario that quantum theory violates with a white-noise tolerance of at least 15% (mathematics-graded).
directions.question: With one observing 'friend' and three settings, is there a test stronger than an ordinary Bell test that quantum theory breaks with noise to spare?
known: The claim that one friend allows nothing beyond Bell tests was stated for two settings only.
A 2024 list of the exceptions seems not to cover one friend with three settings; no such test is published.
directions.cheapest_test: On a laptop, list every boundary of the one-friend, three-setting case, then compute how far quantum theory exceeds each and how much noise it survives; chip only if found.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, P3-8

directions.title: Sequential Peres–Mermin under exact CbD
directions.odds_event: For both input states (|00⟩ and a Bell state), the exact CbD linear program rejects noncontextuality, with CNT2's bootstrap 99% lower bound above 0.
directions.question: On the chip, do answers to nine linked measurements depend on which others are asked with them, even after an exact correction for disturbance?
known: This nine-measurement test has run on Google's chip and on ions, never with the exact disturbance correction.
Program 1 aimed the same correction method at a language model and found nothing beyond chance.
directions.cheapest_test: Measure nine paired quantities one after another in six groups, in both orders and from two starting states (24 circuits x 4,000 shots), then apply the exact disturbance correction.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, P3-9

directions.title: Sequential 4-cycle with the exact KDL criterion
directions.odds_event: The KDL statistic, s_odd(correlators) − Σ|marginal differences|, exceeds 2 with its 99.9% lower bound above 2, in both orders.
directions.question: Does program 1's context-dependence check find context-dependence on the chip, in a loop of four measurements where physics guarantees it?
known: Program 1 used this check on a language model and found 1 of 80 pairs, about what chance gives.
Ion-trap experiments passed the same exact check, by up to 25 standard errors; no superconducting chip has.
directions.cheapest_test: On two qubits plus a helper qubit, measure four quantities in pairs, one after another mid-circuit, in both orders (8 circuits x 4,000 shots), then apply the exact check.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, P3-10

directions.title: Leggett–Garg with MCM, a clumsiness control and CbD
directions.odds_event: For the mixed preparation, both hold: the CbD-corrected K3 exceeds 1 by ≥ 5σ, pooled; and K3 − 1 exceeds the largest measured disturbance on the classical preparations by ≥ 3σ.
directions.question: Does one qubit, checked at three moments, break a limit every everyday object obeys, by more than clumsy measuring could explain?
known: Earlier IBM tests broke the limit, but none measured mid-circuit or fixed a clumsiness check in advance.
An early IBM five-qubit test beat its own measured clumsiness by only about 2.6 standard errors.
directions.cheapest_test: Measure one qubit at three moments as it turns, with clumsiness checks on ordinary starting states: 16 circuits x 4,000 shots, in 6 copies on separate qubits.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, P3-11

directions.title: Do alternating non-commuting measurements show memory?
directions.odds_event: In the alternating circuit, pooled |Corr_κ| < 0.01 at κ = 2, 4 and 6; in the control circuit, consecutive repeats agree ≥ 95% of the time.
directions.question: When a qubit is measured eight times in alternating, incompatible ways, are the outcomes free of any memory of earlier ones?
known: In 2014 Hossenfelder proposed that outcomes could carry a hidden memory lasting about a millionth of a second.
No hardware test of the idea turned up in two literature searches.
directions.cheapest_test: On about 50 separate qubits, measure each eight times alternating two incompatible directions, plus a control measuring one direction eight times: 2 circuits x 4,000 shots.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, P3-12

directions.title: LG-certified randomness from P3-11's data
directions.odds_event: Certified min-entropy ≥ 0.05 bits per round at 99% finite-size confidence, from P3-11's mixed-preparation correlator data.
directions.question: Can the one-qubit, three-moment test also certify its outcomes as truly random, at least 0.05 random bits per round?
known: An IBM version reported no bit count or error bar; a photon version produced 919,118 certified bits.
Choosing the moments uses about 1.58 random bits per round to make at most about 0.11 certified bits.
directions.cheapest_test: Apply a published randomness bound, corrected for finite data, to the one-qubit three-moment test's roughly 72,000 rounds; no extra chip time.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, P3-13

directions.title: Maximally ψ-epistemic models in d = 4, with no fair sampling
directions.odds_event: S + 5σ < 1 under both choices of ωq (intended states and tomography-reconstructed states), on raw counts with no post-selection.
directions.question: Can the chip rule out theories where quantum states overlap only because of our ignorance, counting every result and discarding none?
known: A photon experiment ruled these theories out (score 0.690), but only by assuming lost photons were typical.
A related test (PBR) passed on this chip type, but its threshold came from the authors' own noise model.
directions.cheapest_test: Use two qubits as one four-level system, prepare 5 states and test 10 pairs (30 circuits x 2,000 shots), plus state checks, scoring raw counts with nothing discarded.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, P3-14

directions.title: Gold map direction 11: hardware as an oracle for the engine
directions.diagnosis: Stays closed: here the chip is only a referee, never a resource, and certified randomness from random circuits needs about 2.2 s response time and exascale verification.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: Real versus complex quantum theory
directions.diagnosis: Already settled on IBM hardware twice and on a USTC chip, and truly independent sources are impossible on one chip.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: The PBR theorem
directions.diagnosis: Already passed on a Heron r2 chip (ibm_marrakesh), and preparation independence cannot be guaranteed on one chip.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: Bell test with k redundant friends (Bednorz)
directions.diagnosis: Merged into P3-7, which reports unanimity scoring of the friend qubits at no extra cost.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: Gühne full disturbance-corrected Peres–Mermin inequality
directions.diagnosis: Deferred: a follow-up to P3-9 if it passes, at about 57 QPU s.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: Sorkin test (higher-order interference)
directions.diagnosis: It needs three-level systems (qutrits) or genuine multi-path systems; on qubits it would only test the compiled gates.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: KCBS, Yu–Oh and Lüders-bound Leggett–Garg
directions.diagnosis: They need control of three-level systems (qutrits), which the IBM Open Plan does not give.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: Weak-measurement Leggett–Garg (Rybotycki)
directions.diagnosis: Too costly: about 560 QPU s per job, more than the whole remaining budget.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: Single-qubit Born-rule deviations at 10⁻³
directions.diagnosis: Too costly: it needs 10 to 100 million shots.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: Quantum Darwinism
directions.diagnosis: There is no assumption at stake: it would only demonstrate quantum theory on an engineered environment.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: Quantum switch (indefinite causal order)
directions.diagnosis: A chip runs its gates in a definite order, so simulating the switch tests nothing about causal structure.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: Frauchiger–Renner
directions.diagnosis: On a chip it checks only a Hardy-type probability, while the paradox is about rules of reasoning.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: Measurement-induced phase transitions
directions.diagnosis: Keeping only the wanted runs costs exponentially more as mid-circuit measurements grow, and the transition is a quantum-theory prediction anyway.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: Loophole-free locality or freedom of choice
directions.diagnosis: It needs the parties far apart (spacelike separation), which one chip cannot give.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: Leupold-style sustained sequences
directions.diagnosis: Too costly: about 10 million measurements, against a whole budget of about 1.3 million shots.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: Layer fidelity / EPLG and sparse Pauli–Lindblad learning
directions.diagnosis: IBM already publishes it, the measurement hides systematic error, and learning it costs tens of seconds per layer.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed

directions.title: Direct residual-ZZ or leakage measurement
directions.diagnosis: It needs pulse-level or three-level (qutrit) access, which this plan does not give.
directions.source: nature-graded map/program-3-map.md, Closed, merged and killed
